candidate.blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — transmission-based precautions and PPE
candidate.blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — PPE doffing for airborne precautions
candidate.educational_objective: Apply the CDC location/sequence principle for removing a respirator and other PPE after airborne-isolation care.

options.A: Keep all PPE on until reaching the nurses' station
options.B: Remove the respirator inside the room before removing contaminated gloves and gown
options.C: Remove other PPE before leaving the room or care area; remove the respirator after leaving and closing the door
options.D: Remove PPE in any order and location because hand hygiene eliminates doffing risk

candidate.rationale: CDC Core Infection Prevention Practices state that PPE other than respirators should be removed and discarded after the task and before leaving the patient's room or care area. If a respirator is used, it should be removed after leaving the room/care area and closing the door. C is correct.
candidate.source_claim_supported: PPE other than respirators is removed before leaving the patient's room/care area; respirators are removed after leaving and closing the door.
candidate.source_document_title: Core Infection Prevention and Control Practices for Safe Healthcare Delivery in All Settings
candidate.source_locator: Core Practices Table, 5d Risk Assessment with Appropriate Use of PPE, items 1.4-1.5; lines 111-120 on current page
candidate.source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
candidate.stem: A nurse used a respirator and other PPE while caring for a client in an airborne-infection isolation room. Which removal principle is correct when care is complete?
